references.text: Moses promised the people that the Lord would save them and that they would never see the Egyptians again - this verse shows the fulfillment of that promise.
Israel's song of praise after being saved from the Egyptians at the sea, where they praise the Lord as their salvation and strength.
The psalm describes how the Lord saved Israel at the Red Sea and delivered them from the hand of the enemy.
The psalm tells how God led the people safely while the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
Moses reminds the people what the Lord did to the Egyptian army at the Red Sea.
Joshua recounts the event at the sea where the Lord saved Israel and let them see the Egyptians perish.
Nehemiah describes God's salvation at the Red Sea and how the pursuers were cast into the depths.
Isaiah refers to the Lord's saving of the people at the sea in Moses' days.
The book of Hebrews mentions how the Israelites passed through the Red Sea by faith, while the Egyptians drowned when they tried to do the same.
Stephen's speech refers to Moses leading the people out and performing wonders at the Red Sea.
Both verses refer to the same historical event and emphasize that salvation is a completed work of the Lord on a specific day.
Uses an identical formula for God's salvation ('Thus the Lord saved Israel that day'), showing a theological parallel in how God's intervention is described across history.
A clear theological summary and allusion to the same saving event (the exodus from Egypt) confirming its central role in Israel's history.
Direct allusion to the sea's judgment over the Egyptians as a reminder of God's salvation, linked to leadership in the wilderness.
Prophetic allusion where the exodus from Egypt serves as the prototype for a future, messianic gathering and salvation of God's people.
